claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's just turned 18 and I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you can still claim Child Benefit for Alex now that he's 18.

Since Alex has just turned 18, the key factor is whether he's staying in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, vocational courses, or similar qualifications)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Studying A-levels at sixth form college is considered approved education.

Now I need to understand your current situation a bit better:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now let me ask about your living arrangements with Alex:

**Does Alex currently live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you contributing at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently receiving Child Benefit for him, but I wasn't sure if it would continue now that he's turned 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex working for 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if he's claiming any benefits in his own right - I don't think so, but I'm not certain about that. He's not working 24 hours a week though - he just focuses on his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Based on the rules:
- You normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training
- Alex is 18 years old (under 20) ✓
- He is studying A-levels at sixth form college (approved education) ✓
- He lives with you in the UK ✓
- He is not working 24 hours or more per week ✓

The one area of uncertainty is whether Alex is claiming benefits in his own right. According to the rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts getting certain benefits, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit.

However, since you don't think he's claiming any benefits (which is typical for most 18-year-olds in full-time education living at home), and all other eligibility criteria are clearly met, I can make an assessment.

**Would you like me to provide my eligibility assessment now, or would you prefer to confirm whether Alex is claiming any benefits first?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, please go ahead and provide the assessment now. Like I said, I don't think he's claiming anything - he's just a normal student living at home.

## Eligibility Assessment for Alex

**Good news! You ARE ELIGIBLE to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Here's why:

✅ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 18 years old, which is under the age limit of 20 for children in approved education or training

✅ **Education requirement met**: Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form college, which is considered approved education under Child Benefit rules

✅ **Residence requirement met**: Alex lives at home with you in the UK

✅ **Work status**: Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week (which would stop Child Benefit if he left education)

✅ **Benefits status**: Based on your information, Alex is not claiming benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)

### What this means:

Your Child Benefit should continue automatically as long as Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20 years old. You don't need to make a new claim since you're already receiving it.

### Important things to remember:

- You should notify HMRC if Alex leaves his A-level course or stops being in approved education
- Child Benefit can continue if Alex takes a break and registers with a careers service or the armed services (for up to 20 weeks)
- Once Alex turns 20, Child Benefit will stop regardless of whether he's still in education

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit for Alex?
